title: Playing Snoozer for Whiteman backstage
summary: Brownlee and Hazel borrow a guitar so Whiteman can hear Snoozer, who knocks him out; Hazel recalls how he first met Whiteman.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: But what about Snoozer? You were going to tell about how?

Well, yeah. While they were here, while Whiteman was here, Snoozer was in town. So Brownlee and I, we wanted Whiteman to hear Snoozer, you see. And I had known Whiteman from Tony Perentich, man. I was working at the halfway house with Abby and I was just learning how to play a cornet thing, you see. And I think I knew about four or five tunes. And Abby used to say, you never learn how to play a thing as long as you live. And I told him, I'll see the day when I was stuck like that, you know. And they used to stagger for lunch in Perentich, man. In other words, one man at a time off the stand for lunch. And Henry Connect was playing cornet. Well, he was strictly a legitimate cornet, no jazz at all, you see. So I'd get off at one o'clock at the halfway house, you see. I'd just get in time to relieve Henry to go for lunch, you see. And we'd play the four tunes that I knew, you see. And Whiteman happened to come in town one time and he was there and he heard me playing. He asked Tony Perentich, who's the guy playing the jazz, you see. And then Tony said, yeah, the carnet plays the drum. He plays out with Abby Bruce out there. He said, just learned how to play a carnet. Well, Paul came up and he complimented me on the horn, you see. Well, anyway, Brownlee and I called Paul and told him we wanted him to hear this Snoozer, you see. So Snoozer didn't have a guitar. He didn't bring a guitar with him. So we went up to the hotel, to the Biennale and got Joe Capriero's guitar. And we brought it and we went backstage. You see, we had Snoozer play for Whiteman. And then he knocked Whiteman out. And Whiteman would listen, he'd play a thing, especially that day. Did you ever say I used to play Tiger Rag? No. He'd wave his hands like this and he'd play with his fingers, pick with his fingers, you know. He wouldn't even touch the strings with this hand. He'd be waving there and he'd make a break, you know. And the damnedest things would come out of that thing, Bill. I believe Johnny's got some, Wiggs has got some on record, yeah. He got some on record.
Not that one, but some of the others.

Whiteman would listen, man, and he'd run up and they had a, the theater was a brick wall. And he wanted me to hit his shoulder up against him, boom, against that brick wall like that, you know, every time Snoozer would knock him out.
